title: Cartesian pullback of an infinity-category localization
statement: Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small infinity-category and let $W\subseteq\mathcal C$ be a subcategory containing every equivalence. Suppose $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a localization at $W$: for every infinity-category $\mathcal T$, restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal T)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal T)$ on functors carrying $W$ to equivalences, including all mapping spaces. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be a Cartesian fibration, meaning an inner fibration (a simplicial map having the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion) with Cartesian lifts of every base arrow with specified target. An edge $e:E'\to E$ is Cartesian when, for every $Z$, the square of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(Z,E')\to\operatorname{Map}(Z,E)$ over $\operatorname{Map}(pZ,pE')\to\operatorname{Map}(pZ,pE)$ is a homotopy pullback. Form the pullback $\mathcal E'=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal E$ in infinity-categories. Let $T$ consist of the arrows of $\mathcal E'$ whose image in $\mathcal C$ is in $W$ and whose image in $\mathcal E$ is an equivalence. Then the projection $\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ exhibits $\mathcal E$ as the localization $\mathcal E'[T^{-1}]_\infty$. This asserts the same functor-category universal property, including all mapping spaces, for every target $\mathcal T$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.16 (canonical localization pushout of Remark 5.3.13); Lemma 5.3.15 Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Choose the groupoid completion $\eta:W\to\kappa W$ of [lem-coef-localization-kan-cartesian-fibration]. The identity of $\kappa W$ is Cartesian: every mapping-space test square for an edge is a square with identity vertical maps, and that edge itself is the required lift. Apply that lemma with $\mathcal F=\kappa W$ and $\pi=\mathrm{id}$. Every edge of the Kan complex $\kappa W$ is an equivalence: filling the two outer 2-horns supplies left and right homotopy inverses. Thus it follows that restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\kappa W,\mathcal T)\to\operatorname{Fun}(W,\mathcal T)$ is fully faithful with essential image the functors inverting every arrow of $W$. The restriction of $q$ to $W$ therefore extends to $\kappa W\to\mathcal D$, with a coherent agreement on $W$. Form $P=\mathcal C\amalg_W\kappa W$ using [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout]. Its displayed functor-category pullback formula identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal T)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal T)$ inverting $W$. The assumed universal property of $q$ gives the same subcategory for $\mathcal D$. Explicitly the maps $P\to\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal D\to P$ extending the two localization cocones are mutually inverse: full faithfulness of restriction makes each composite equivalent to the identity. Thus $W\to\kappa W$, $\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a pushout square. Here $q$ is its bottom arrow.

source.place: Definition 5.3.11, Remark 5.3.13 and Proposition 5.3.16 setup; canonical-square argument written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-localization-cartesian-pullback-pushout] with $A=W$, $B=\kappa W$, $C=\mathcal C$, $D=\mathcal D$, and $E=\mathcal E$. Write $A'=W\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal E$ and $B'=\kappa W\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal E$. The resulting square $A'\to B'$, $\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ is a pushout. The coherent composite $\kappa W\to\mathcal D$ is the one obtained in step 1; no assertion that an arbitrary pullback preserves pushouts is being made.

The projection $B'\to\kappa W$ is Cartesian. To verify this directly, pull a Cartesian lift in $\mathcal E$ back together with its specified base arrow in $\kappa W$; its mapping-space square is obtained by pulling back the Cartesian mapping-space square in $\mathcal E$, hence is again a homotopy pullback. Inner-horn lifting also pulls back. With $W\times_{\kappa W}B'\simeq A'$, apply [lem-coef-localization-kan-cartesian-fibration]. It says that $A'\to B'$ is the localization at the class $S$ of arrows whose image in $B'$ is an equivalence. An arrow in $B'$ is an equivalence precisely when its two components are: componentwise inverses, together with the pulled-back compatibility homotopy, give its inverse in the pullback. Its $\kappa W$ component is always an equivalence, so $S$ consists precisely of arrows of $A'$ whose $\mathcal E$ component is an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.16 proof, second paragraph using Lemma 5.3.15; base-change and equivalence checks written out

proof.text:
For any target $\mathcal T$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout] to the pushout of step 2:
$$\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal T)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E',\mathcal T)\times^h_{\operatorname{Fun}(A',\mathcal T)}\operatorname{Fun}(B',\mathcal T).$$
By step 3 the last restriction is fully faithful with essential image the $S$-inverting functors. Its pullback is therefore fully faithful with essential image those $F:\mathcal E'\to\mathcal T$ whose restriction to $A'$ inverts $S$: for each such $F$, the space of an extension on $B'$ together with an identification on $A'$ is contractible. For two compatible pairs $(F,G,\alpha)$ and $(F_1,G_1,\alpha_1)$, their mapping space is
$$\operatorname{Map}(F,F_1)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(F|_{A'},F_1|_{A'})}\operatorname{Map}(G,G_1),$$
where the second map uses $\alpha,\alpha_1$ to identify the restrictions of $G,G_1$. Full faithfulness of restriction from $B'$ makes that second map an equivalence, so this homotopy pullback maps equivalently to $\operatorname{Map}(F,F_1)$. This checks the full mapping spaces, including the noninvertible transformations. Finally $A'\simeq W\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal E'$; because $W\subseteq\mathcal C$ is a subcategory, its arrows are exactly the arrows of $\mathcal E'$ over $W$. Step 3 identifies the image of $S$ among them with the arrows whose $\mathcal E$ component is an equivalence. This image is exactly $T$. Thus the displayed comparison is the required restriction functor and its essential image is precisely the $T$-inverting functors, with all mapping spaces retained.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.16 proof, final pasting argument expanded as a full functor-category computation

lean.statement: theorem localization_cartesian_pullback {C D E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory C] [Quasicategory D] [Quasicategory E] (W : C.Subcomplex) (_hW : InnerFibration W.ι) (_hEquivalences : ∀ e : C _⦋1⦌, IsEquivalenceEdge C e → e ∈ W.obj (op ⦋1⦌)) (q : C ⟶ D) (_hq : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} q (W.obj (op ⦋1⦌))) (p : E ⟶ D) (_hp : cartesianFibration p) : IsLocalizationAtEdges.{u, v} (pullback.snd q p) {e | (pullback.fst q p).app _ e ∈ W.obj (op ⦋1⦌) ∧ IsEquivalenceEdge E ((pullback.snd q p).app _ e)}
lean.note: Uses the existing full functor-category IsLocalizationAtEdges predicate with arbitrary containing target universe. The subcategory W is a simplicial subset whose inclusion is an inner fibration (Kerodon Definition 4.1.2.2), with every equivalence included. Cartesian fibrations use the recorded horn interface, equivalent to the stated mapping-space criterion by HTT 2.4.4.3. Its strict pullback models the infinity-categorical pullback by HTT 3.3.1.4. No auxiliary notion is redefined; stmt_deps gains the landed localization definition.
